newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes firm amid talk of NYMEX delivery.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes firm amid talk of NYMEX delivery.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes were firm on Wednesday afternoon amid ongoing talk that a foreign crude would be delivered into the NYMEX this month, traders said.

Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) have been commanding a premium recently as traders attempt to shift out of paper positions to avoid the uncertainty of receiving a crude other than West Texas Intermediate/Cushing upon expiry next Tuesday, traders said.
Traders said either North Sea Brent or Nigerian Bonny Light could be delivered. "The feeling is that something foreign will get delivered," a Gulf Coast trader said.
A Brent delivery would give the buyer a discount of 30 cents a barrel to WTI/Cushing, while Bonny Light would entail a premium of 60 cents a barrel.
The possible delivery is seen as a bearish signal, since NYMEX is considered the home of last resort for most sellers.
Meanwhile, sour crude continued to retain its robust tone despite the full reopening of all Mexican crude ports that had been closed due to severe weather.
The strength was attributed to pent-up refinery demand as well as the fallout of the outage at the Shell-operated Mars production platform in the Gulf of Mexico.
The deep-water platform was gradually coming back on stream after an electrical glitch shut down operations last Friday.

West Texas Sour/Midland was hovering around $2.03-1.90 a barrel under WTI/Cushing, with no deals heard transacted as the market digested the psychological leap into above-$2.00 territory, traders said.
Eugene Island was wide at WTI/Cushing minus $1.95-75 barrel.
Thinly traded Bonito Sour was dealt at minus $1.20 a barrel.
Among sweet grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James moved higher to minus 30-27 cents. The grade was heard done at minus 28, 29, 30 and 32 cents a barrel.
WTI/Midland was even at minus 32-30 cents, with minus 31 and 30 cents getting done earlier today, traders said.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was firmer at minus 90-85 cents a barrel.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus changed hands at $1.85, traders said.
